Very disappointing and unprofessional experience regarding an export transaction for a Porsche Panamera.

We worked on this deal for more than a week, invested a significant amount of time, energy and professional resources, and provided every single document requested by their financial department step by step.

Each time new requirements were added: company documents, bank confirmations, ID verification, payment proofs, transport conditions, etc. We complied with everything in complete transparency and good faith.

Despite this, after days of discussions and document requests, the transaction was suddenly refused with vague explanations about “internal policies” and “third party transactions”, even though the purchasing company was a legitimate German GmbH car dealer company buying the vehicle for its own stock.

What is most problematic is not the refusal itself, but the way the file was handled:

constant changes in requirements,
lack of clarity from the beginning,
repeated requests for documents while the deal was apparently already viewed negatively internally,
and a complete waste of time and business resources for all parties involved.

Even when we explained that transport conditions could be adapted to fully match their requirements, the discussion was abruptly closed.

As automotive professionals working internationally, we find this export process management extremely disappointing and unnecessarily complicated.

I sincerely hope we can still find a professional solution together. If the situation evolves positively and a fair solution is found, I will of course remove or update this review accordingly.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wish I had read about other people's experiences with this company before I chose mSpa, because you should avoid both the company and the products like the plague!

In order not to make a long story that will be just as boring to read as it was to experience, we can summarize it like this:

What was good:
- Kenneth (Salesman or owner, I think) was nice and I still want to say that I think he reasons logically and is customer-focused.

The bad:
- Their biggest problem is Johan (the support) who is very nonchalant and frighteningly ignorant in the area he supports.
- If you do as Johan says, you will harm both your spa and your guests because he takes every answer you get and very often contradicts himself.
- If you ask a follow-up question about something that doesn't seem to match what he previously said, you will either get cocky answers back that you are "thinking too much" or he will just close the matter and give you a hard time.

So what happened:
In short, the bath broke within a year and it cost me a lot to troubleshoot it myself (the support does not value what it costs you in time or money). They found ONE reason that results in what they saw during the repair but completely missed most of the other things that could cause this and the evidence that spoke against their conclusion (including the evidence that the bath was crap from the beginning but Johan didn't care then either and thought it was annoying to hear back when they had already received their money).
I was down at Folkpool who got to look at the pictures and read the dialogues with mSpa and they absolutely did not agree with mSpa's conclusion.

Conclusion:
If Johan himself had read any of the material he himself refers to, he would have understood much more about water chemistry and maintenance.

You should choose mSpa in Kungälv if you want:
- Endless email dialogues without getting any real answers.
- Constantly having to remind you of questions that are never read and answers that are not provided.
- A product of really low quality (you definitely get less per kroner here than with the cheapest competitor).
- At least two or three deliveries per item that is supposed to be sent before they actually manage to send the correct one (often things are missing completely).
- Get back a "repaired" product that now sounds worse and more damaged than before it went in for repair.

Please buy STIHL from a reputable dealer – but avoid buying directly from STIHL.

I visited Emporia's Information Desk to get help with a situation where an ATM had withdrawn money from my account without giving out any cash.

I didn't expect the information desk to be able to resolve the banking issue, but I did expect them to at least be able to provide basic guidance on who to contact or how to proceed when something like this happens.

Instead, I was met with a defensive attitude and was told to go back to the ATM to see which bank owned it, as the information desk has no information about it. "It must say the name of the bank on the ATM," she meant.

When we went to the ATM together, it turned out that no specific bank was listed, even after she asked me to insert my card again. It said "BANKOMAT". Despite this, I couldn't get any information about where to turn or what phone number I could contact.

What surprised me most was that the conversation then turned to the fact that "Swedes don't use cash anymore" and pay with their mobile phones. I didn't understand the relevance of this statement at all.

I am Swedish myself (despite my Asian appearance) and use cash when necessary, especially when traveling. Above all, I was there as a customer with a specific problem and not to discuss how different groups of people choose to pay.

In a multicultural city like Malmö, I think such generalizations are both unnecessary and inappropriate. Regardless of background or appearance, you should be treated as a customer and receive help based on your case.

When I then asked who I could contact to express my views on the information desk service, the person I spoke to stated that she herself was the owner of the company that runs the information desk at Emporia. I therefore felt that there was no clear opportunity to raise the issue further or have my views tested by someone else in charge.

I appreciate that she went with me to the ATM to try to help, but I still left the information desk without any concrete guidance on how to handle the problem.

For an information desk in one of Sweden's largest shopping centers, I would have expected a more solution-oriented approach, better knowledge of where visitors can be referred for this type of problem, and a greater focus on the customer's question rather than on irrelevant generalizations.

WARNING FRAUD/CAR BUYER
I want to issue a serious warning against this company. Almost 2 weeks ago I found a Jeep Wrangler for sale at Varbergs Bilcenter. On April 23, I went down to the car dealership to look at the car after receiving information from the company that the car was in very good condition. There was only a little surface rust on the door hinges and the car was in better condition than normal according to the seller. Advertised price 429,900 SEK, model year 2020 (later it turned out that it was from 2019) and only 8000 km on the odometer. Upon arrival, the car was very dirty. There were clear signs that the car had been used for off-road driving. According to the seller, the car had not been used for off-road driving. When I examined the car, there were clear signs that refuted this, scuffs, scratches in the paint, fenders, scuffs and damage to the undercarriage, wheel axles, suspension, front end, wheel arches, etc., which are common when driving off-road. These damages had started to rust heavily. During a test drive, strong vibrations were discovered from the right front wheel. According to the seller, this was due to rough-patterned tires. This was probably due to incorrect wheel alignment or something much worse. When checking with a fault code reader, it was discovered that several previous fault codes had probably been erased. During the test drive, fault messages were also discovered on the dashboard that appeared and then disappeared. I got a very bad overall impression of the car and that the seller was trying to hide something. I had driven 600 km one-way with very high expectations where I was set on buying the car. Upon arrival, it turned out to be something completely different. When I confronted the seller about the defects, he denied everything and made up various excuses. I got a very bad feeling about Varbergs Bilcenter. The car purchase did not happen and I would especially like to warn you who were thinking of buying a car from Varbergs Bilcenter to turn to another more serious car dealer.

I want to share a very serious experience at the emergency room in Trollhättan (NÄL).

Three days ago I contacted the emergency center due to clear and serious symptoms – I was urinating extremely frequently (over eight times during the night), was constantly thirsty and felt that something was seriously wrong. The emergency center and 1177 assessed the situation as urgent and wanted to send an ambulance, but due to a lack of available ambulances, I had to be driven to the emergency room by my sister instead. They were clear that I had to go in immediately.

When I got to the emergency room, I informed the staff about exactly these symptoms, as well as about my kidney failure and my medications. Despite this, no tests were taken. No blood sugar was checked, no blood samples were taken, and I was sent home without a proper examination.

The next day my condition deteriorated further. I then sought help via the emergency center where it was immediately determined that my blood sugar was very high. I was sent back to the hospital urgently – and only then did I receive the right care.

The doctors who treated me reacted to the fact that I had previously been sent home in that condition.

This is not just negligence – it is a serious lack of patient safety. I could have suffered very serious consequences, including vision loss or worse.

What makes the situation even more worrying is that the staff did not take responsibility afterwards, but instead referred the matter to each other.

I really hope that this criticism is taken seriously. Patients must be listened to, especially when both symptoms and the emergency center point to an acute condition. Basic checks such as blood sugar must not be ignored in the face of such clear warning signs.

This must not happen again.

I don’t know if I’ve ever spent this much time in the ER anywhere else—diagnosis was made 2 hours after arrival, and after 5 hours I’m still waiting for a doctor to see me and confirm what the nurse said. If you need medical help, call an ambulance, because here you’re more likely to die than get help.

Unfortunately, time ran out to file a report with ARN.

I asked TWO different employees about the price for the follow-up vaccination of our cat TWICE on different occasions, and got the same answer from both. Completely without the 340 kronor that was later added.

My impression is that the manager started the business entirely to maximize profits. Shabby premises and lower wages out in the country, as well as somewhat arbitrary prices, are not trustworthy, but in the veterinary industry, most pet owners are in an emergency situation, and do not dare to question what it costs.

At the first visit, which concerned the same cat whose eye was mildly infected, more than ten items ended up on the invoice. Everything from the cost (200?) to write a prescription, to small pieces of paper to wash the eye, which cost 8 kronor each.

Now we have found competent and pleasant veterinarians, for all our animals, elsewhere.

Avoid this veterinarian. Sooner or later your animal will be mistreated, and if you complain…

But if you want to pay more than you get, you've come to the right place.

If you are unlucky enough to have Ellevio as your electricity company, I just want to apologize.
This is probably one of the worst and worst companies in all of Sweden.
The only thing that allows them to continue is because they have a monopoly (or oligopoly might be more appropriate) on the electricity network.
Price increases and the like are part of everyday life with this company.
As an example, we can take our household.
In February 2025, our house consumed about 231kWh, which cost us 692 SEK.
Then compare that with May 2021 when we consumed 538kWh and it cost 613 SEK!
I have attached pictures that confirm this.
We have more than halved our consumption, so to speak, but it still costs us more? For example, Ellevio's subscription fee, which cost 240kr in 2021, but costs 365kr in 2025 (they took the opportunity to increase it at the same time as they also added the power tariff).
If you compare it to how prices have gone up and inflation, it should be about 21% higher, but Ellevio secures its profits by raising its prices by about 52% during the same period!
Also add the completely screwed-up solution with the "power tariff" which must indeed be introduced according to the Energy Agency, but not until January 1, 2027, but Ellevio of course wants to protect the environment and is introducing it now (*cough money *cough).
So even though we have reduced our total electricity consumption from about 8400kwh in 2021 to about 3400kwh in 2024, we still have to pay more to Ellevio.
It can be mentioned that at the same time they send out a survey to their customers that doesn't work (a way to get rid of bad reviews?).
What we are working towards is being able to go completely off-grid just to be able to avoid this extremely sick company when we cancel the subscription.
Because don't think that prices will go down at all, they will only go up.
If you could give 0 stars, it would have been better.

I drove in and started vacuuming; I always want to do it before the wash so that the car doesn't get dusty afterwards. I take them out and meet her who is very upset and tells me sharply that "vacuum cleaning is only for customers"! I don't really understand because I am a customer and I explain it to her. I explain that I always vacuum first and then wash because I don't want the car to get dusty afterwards. She understands the situation and says it's OK for me to drive into the car wash afterwards but continues to angrily tell me about everyone who vacuums and skips, washcloths that get stolen, etc. Why should I have to listen to that?! I point out that I don't appreciate being jumped on like this when I'm a regular customer who intended to do the right thing for me. She says several times, however, that "you have to understand that, that we'll tell you". No, I don't.

I've been washing my car here for several years and am always completely satisfied. This was the last time, though. I'll have to look for another place that really is a "nice car wash" as it says on your sign.

I advise all dog owners not to take a course at the dog academy.
The instructors do not base the course content on modern science and many of the methods are based on physical violence.
For example, we course participants were instructed to use a choke chain on the dogs and to correct the dog by jerking when it pulled on the leash. If the dog did not show clear submission in the form of ears lying back, a low posture and the tail between the legs, the handler has not corrected his dog hard enough and must act more forcefully.
On one occasion, we witnessed a course participant who pushed his dog down and lay on top of it when it did not listen to a command and where the instructor urged the course participant to hold the dog in that position for a longer time to ensure that the dog really felt that it was being punished. The communication from the instructors was very manipulative and there was absolutely no pleasant atmosphere. During the theoretical parts, many examples were also given of situations where physical violence and punishments were used. For example, one instructor tells of having had to correct her own dog "properly" on various occasions and that she even staged a situation with the aim of punishing her dog. Then she had put out a sandwich, shown the dog the sandwich, walked away and with the help of a mirror saw when the dog was about to take it and then flew at the dog and physically grabbed it and she herself describes how scared the dog became at that incident without feeling any remorse, shame or understanding of why it is very problematic to act in that way.
There was also talk of how the instructors had "helped" another team with their reactive dog by throwing a can full of gravel at it. Unfortunately, the list is long and these are just a few examples of the disgusting methods the dog academy advocates.
Fortunately, I know better myself, of course we questioned the methods and absolutely did not subject our dog to any of these abuses. Unfortunately, the instructors were also not familiar with the terminology of basic learning theory, research, or willing to discuss/consider research, so it was impossible to get anywhere. We ultimately chose to simply cancel the course and go home.
If you have a dog and want him or her to feel good, whether it's training or upbringing, choose another place, absolutely don't go here! There is no reason whatsoever why you should have to use force to achieve either upbringing or obedience.

Hi,

I placed an order with Toolab￼ on May 7th — a tool kit and some smaller accessories, for a total of about 15,000 SEK. It wasn’t a huge order, but the tools were needed for a job outside the city where I live.

What’s very frustrating is that the entire order was left waiting for a small detail that I didn’t even need urgently. Today I have to go to the job site, but the tools won’t arrive until Monday. And this despite two phone calls during the week. After the first call, nothing happened at all — the order wasn’t split up and wasn’t shipped.

Now I’m forced to borrow tools from friends because what I ordered almost two weeks ago still hasn’t arrived.

Unfortunately, I feel like this has become very common in Sweden. You see “delivery 2–5 days” on the website, but in practice you often have to wait significantly longer. It feels like orders are being held back to coordinate deliveries and reduce costs, instead of sending what’s actually in stock right away.

For those of us who work with tools, this is not just an annoyance — it costs money. Tools are what I work with and earn my living from. When deliveries don't work, you lose work time and income.

The most disappointing thing is perhaps the lack of accountability. No apology, no compensation, no solution despite the problem being brought to our attention several times.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this store after this experience, and I will not shop here again. I will also not recommend the company to others in the industry, as delays like these create downtime and costs for businesses.

Very bad experience. If I could give 0 stars, I would.

one_star_reviews.text: My friend went to this restaurant and found this in her food. ❌❌❌❌❌❌❗️❗️❗️❗️

We were a group of four who visited Pasta+ with the expectation of a nice dinner, but unfortunately the experience was anything but good.

Right from the start, there were problems with our voucher. We clearly asked the man who welcomed us if the voucher was valid for the whole group, which he confirmed that it was. Later, a female employee claimed the opposite and refused to listen to our explanation or even check with her colleague who had given us the information. This created an unnecessary and frustrating situation, and the service was consistently unprofessional.

Unfortunately, the food was no better. Two of us ordered truffle pasta with mushrooms, but both dishes were extremely salty, so much so that it completely took over the taste. There was no hint of truffle, even though it was a main component of the dish. We pointed this out, but were met with no reaction, not even an offer to fix the problem.

The other two in the group ordered scampi pasta. Unfortunately, these dishes were not a positive experience either. The taste was weak and did not live up to expectations, especially when it came to seafood. In addition, both dishes contained mussels that were not only bad, but also had broken pieces of mussel shell left in the food, something that absolutely should not occur and that makes it directly unacceptable from both a quality and safety point of view. It simply should not have even passed through the kitchen.

Overall, we can conclude that this was a very bad experience, both in terms of service and the food itself. Considering that the bill ended up at around 800 SEK, it feels like money completely wasted. Pasta+ has gotten significantly worse in recent years. When you read positive reviews today, it is difficult to understand what they are based on, since our experience did not reflect any of what others describe. On the contrary, the overall impression was consistently negative.

We expected significantly more, and it is difficult not to feel that you could just as easily have cooked better pasta at home.
